::: {.why}
You have conditioned an ill-behaved covariance matrix before under another name, so the useful content here is what the target is and how the intensity is chosen, not why shrinkage works.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage target and the criterion that sets the intensity, and say what the intensity depends on.
- Explain the method in one sentence to someone who works on linkage disequilibrium matrices.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement the estimator yourself before calling the library: shrink toward a scaled identity, and choose the intensity by minimising the expected squared Frobenius distance to the true matrix using the analytic estimate. Then check your intensity against sklearn's LedoitWolf on the same data. Agreement to two decimals means you understood it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Compare targets: run the same out-of-sample risk test as yesterday for shrinkage toward the identity, toward a constant-correlation matrix, and toward a single-factor matrix. Report predicted and realised risk for all three plus the clipped estimator.
:::
:::
